title: Proposal
description: A case put to someone who decides, before any code: a bid or pitch to a client, or a change put to the company's leadership. It holds the needs and how each is answered, the options, a range estimate, the assumptions, exclusions, risks, and open questions, and the two human decisions: go or no-go, and the sign-off before it is sent. Once accepted, `aidd proposal convert` turns it into an Initiative and Epics that trace back to it.

audience.description: `client`: a bid, pitch, or response to a request for proposal. `internal`: a change put to the company's own decision makers, such as leadership, an investment committee, or an architecture board.

addressee.description: Who receives the proposal and decides, such as "Acme Corp procurement" or "the executive committee".

goal.description: What the addressee gets if they say yes, as an outcome they can check.

status.description: exploring: qualifying, before the go/no-go decision. no_go: a person decided not to pursue it. drafting: a person decided to go. ready: a person signed it off. submitted: sent to the addressee. accepted, rejected, or withdrawn: the outcome.

confidential.description: The material stays in this proposal's folder and is never reused for another addressee without permission. Default true.

go_no_go.description: The first human decision: pursue it or not, before the team spends effort drafting.

by.description: The person who decided, such as @lead. Never an agent.

sign_off.description: The second human decision: the proposal may be sent, with its price, commitments, assumptions, and exclusions.

by.description: The person who signed it off. Never an agent.

needs.description: What the addressee needs, one entry each, and how the proposal answers it: the compliance matrix of a bid, or the concerns a business case must meet.

source.description: Where the need comes from, such as "RFP 3.2" or "CFO, 2026-09-01".

answer.description: met, partly_met (say what is missing), alternative (a different way to the same end), or not_met (say why).

epic.description: The Epic this need belongs to once accepted; `aidd proposal convert` groups needs by it.

options.description: The real alternatives, doing nothing included when it is one.

estimate.description: A range, never a single number: low, most likely, and high, and what it rests on.

unit.description: Such as person-days, person-weeks, or EUR.

basis.description: What the range rests on: comparable past work, `aidd metrics` lead times, or a breakdown.

assumptions.description: What must hold for the proposal to stand. Each is a risk if it turns out false.

exclusions.description: What the proposal does not include, said plainly.

questions.description: Questions for the addressee, with the answer once known: the clarification log.
